source.title: Balanced Multimodal Learning via On-the-fly Gradient Modulation
source.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2022)

confidence_rationale: Independent group, independent method, same conclusion as Wu et al. 2022: under a uniform objective a dominant pathway leaves the others under-optimised, and adaptively damping the dominant pathway's gradient according to its contribution lead rescues them. This is almost literally MECH-333's 'suppress the dominant scoring pathway's effective update magnitude'. Held at 0.6 because the authors needed injected Gaussian noise to stop gradient suppression from hurting generalization -- a real caveat on naive suppression -- and because there is no developmental window or closure.
failure_signatures: Gradient modulation alone risked a generalization drop; the authors added dynamically varying Gaussian noise to compensate, so suppressing the dominant pathway is not free and needs an exploration/regularisation partner.

Modulation is continuous and contribution-driven for the whole of training, not a time-bounded window with a closure event, so the result says nothing about whether balance persists once suppression is lifted.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Multimodal discriminative models with a uniform objective for all modalities can leave uni-modal representations under-optimised because another modality dominates. On-the-fly gradient modulation adaptively controls each modality's optimisation by monitoring the discrepancy in their contribution to the objective; a dynamically changing Gaussian noise term is added to avoid a generalization drop caused by the modulation. The method improves over common fusion methods and boosts existing multimodal methods.
mapping.ree_translation: OGM-GE is a working instance of MECH-333's operation: measure which pathway is winning, scale down its gradient in proportion, let the losers catch up. Mapped to REE, F plays the dominant modality and the gated-policy diversity heads play the under-optimised ones. The added noise term is a useful design hint -- suppression of the winner may need a paired diversity-injection signal, which REE would source from the babbling/curiosity machinery rather than Gaussian noise.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Supervised audio-visual classification, not action selection. The contribution-discrepancy signal is available because there is a label; REE's analogue (how much F vs a diversity head contributed to a good commitment) is far noisier. No phases, no release, no crystallization, so only the open-window half of ARC-075 is addressed.
mapping.source_context: Supervised audio-visual and multimodal classification benchmarks; CVPR 2022 oral with public code.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue, public code, replicates the Wu et al. phenomenon with a different remedy. Mapping to MECH-333 is unusually literal at the operator level; the developmental structure of ARC-075 is absent.
